answer: Every agent must lock a refundable deposit in a shared atlas registry before transacting: the atlas binds each verified identity to exactly one stake, and falcon-style random audits challenge live agents to prove a unique hardware-backed key within minutes. A thousand fake identities means a thousand locked deposits and a thousand keys kept ready to answer; a failed audit slashes the deposit, so a sybil farm pays full stake per identity while honest agents pay only a temporary lock. The registry stays a haven for real participants: faking costs scale linearly with the attack.
